voice.vocabulary_level: Write up. Assume intelligent, sophisticated reader. Never condescend.
voice.sentence_style: Short and punchy by default. Considered and layered for long-form.
voice.philosophy: Teach, demonstrate, make them reach for it. Never sell. Never push.

say_the_uncomfortable_thing.description: Find the market truth everyone knows but nobody says, and say it first.

show_your_work.description: Transparency about methodology is more disruptive than any bold claim.

have_a_point_of_view.description: Every piece must contain a clear, arguable perspective.

punch_at_the_category.description: Challenge the old way of doing things. Never name competitors.

respect_the_reader.description: Write up. Assume sophistication. Never condescend.

category_norms_to_break: Professional tools should be enterprise-priced and enterprise-sold
Workforce data should be priced per record, scaling with company size
AI outputs should look confident even when fabricated
Consulting methodology should be a black box that justifies opacity
PMO tools should require weeks of configuration before delivering value
Trading education should come from gurus who claim to never lose

visual.image_style: Data visualisation and clean diagrams over stock photography. Dark backgrounds.
visual.video_aesthetic: Talking head with data overlay. Clean B-roll of screens and dashboards. On-screen text for key stats. No flashy transitions.

cta_standards.linkedin: Soft question or discussion prompt. Never 'sign up now'.
cta_standards.reddit: No CTA. Value only. Link in profile if asked.
cta_standards.email: Single clear action. Never multiple CTAs.
cta_standards.substack: Reply to this email. Or: early access mention, understated.
cta_standards.twitter: Thread ends with perspective, not pitch.

disclosure_requirements: ATLAS: 'This is a research tool, not financial advice' on all trading content
AI-generated content: No disclosure required (it's our methodology, not a deception)
Data sources: Always cite when using public data
Affiliate/sponsored: Not applicable (no paid promotion model)

approval_workflow.auto_approve: Content above quality threshold passing benchmark check
always_require_approval: Content claiming specific returns or outcomes

positioning.tagline: Clear, evidence-first thinking on business, strategy and leadership — pragmatic over academic.
positioning.enemy: Empty expertise — confident opinions dressed up as insight, complexity sold as rigour, and strategy that never survives contact with reality. (Big-consulting theatre is one example of it, not the whole enemy.)
positioning.thesis: Think clearly, act pragmatically, show the working. The best strategy is the one that actually ships — grounded in the real economics of how businesses grow and how people actually behave, not in academic frameworks.
positioning.audience: Operators, founders and leaders who have to actually deliver — done paying for confident opinions with no evidence behind them.

pillars.name: Clear thinking & better decisions
pillars.desc: Mental models, judgement, and avoiding smart-sounding mistakes.

pillars.name: Real economics of growth
pillars.desc: What actually moves a business versus what gets billed for.

pillars.name: Strategy that ships
pillars.desc: The gap between the deck and the doing — execution in the real world.

pillars.name: Leadership & the human side
pillars.desc: Politics, incentives, and getting people to actually move.

pillars.name: The complexity tax
pillars.desc: Where hidden complexity quietly costs money and speed — one angle, not the whole story.

pillars.name: Show the working
pillars.desc: Transparent teardowns with the evidence attached — proof over posturing.
